dial.summary: Global M2 sustained at $102.7T and Fed balance sheet confirmed at $6.75T (July 22 H.4.1) provide the macro liquidity floor; with BTC.D at 56.52%, TOTAL at $2.27T, and funding rates near-zero (+0.006%/8h), the structural accumulation setup holds intact ahead of the July 28–29 FOMC decision—the primary near-term catalyst needed to break DXY below 100 and compress real yields toward the 2% neutral threshold.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at approximately $102.7T per MacroMicro series (May 2026 vintage, confirmed at $102,653B per latest update); US M2 (H.6, June 2026): $21.94T—Fed implemented new IRA/Keogh methodology in July 28 H.6 release adding ~$1T to reported value; China M2 ~$50T growing ~9% YoY; EU M2 ~$19.4T; Japan ~$9T; Mises Institute confirms money supply growth in 2026 at multi-year high; 4-week trend up: global M2 uptrend sustained across all major components, YoY growth positive and accelerating; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; contracting-YoY headwind condition not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: June 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 53.3%, released July 1—sixth consecutive expansion month, 0.7pp below May's 54.0%; July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI releases Monday August 3, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—first major Q3 data point and first significant release post-FOMC (July 29 decision); sub-indicators from June: new orders 56.0% (-0.8pp), production 52.2% (-2.1pp), employment 49.7% (contracting), prices paid 73.0% (-9.1pp, largest single-month drop since July 2022); 4-week trend down (May 54.0% → June 53.3%); status neutral (above 50 but falling—supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot on July 26, 2026: 101.465 per current market data; June 25, 2026 close confirmed at 101.43 (per ChainCatcher/Vantage Markets); 4-week trend flat: DXY moved from 101.43 (June 25 close) to 101.47 (July 26)—change of +0.04%, well within the <0.5% relative flat threshold; DXY has traded in a 101.3–101.5 range through late July; status headwind (ICE DXY above the 100 threshold; July 28–29 FOMC dovish guidance is the primary near-term catalyst for a sustained break below 100; supportive threshold is DXY below 97.5).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) confirmed at 2.37% as of July 21–24, 2026 (MacroRadar/FRED; up 4.9% over past 12 months); 10Y nominal at 4.67% on July 24 close (2Y at 4.33%), implying breakeven ~2.30%; FRED DFII10 direct API proxy-blocked; 4-week trend up: DFII10 rose approximately +0.19pp from ~2.18% on June 25 to 2.37% on July 21—well above the 5bp flat threshold; status headwind (above 2% and rising on 4-week basis; July 30 Q2 GDP advance and June PCE are the next disinflation tests).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 10-year Treasury at 4.67% (July 24 close, latest available—July 25–26 are weekend); 2-year at 4.33% (July 24 close confirmed); spread: 4.67% − 4.33% = +0.34%; updated from prior run's +0.36% as 10Y eased 2bps from the July 23 close; 4-week trend flat: spread was approximately +0.39–0.40% on June 25, now +0.34%—narrowing of ~5–6bps, near the 5bp flat boundary; status neutral (positive spread well clear of the −50bps deep-inversion headwind threshold; not steepening on 30-day basis; July 28–29 FOMC dovish guidance is primary near-term catalyst for steepening).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL confirmed at $6.75T for week ending July 22, 2026 (per Convex/FRED H.4.1 data, released July 24); updated from prior run's estimated $6.74T; next H.4.1 release July 30, 2026 (week ending July 29); 4-week trend flat: balance sheet moved from approximately $6.72T (late June) to $6.75T (July 22)—change of ~+$0.03T (+0.45%), within the flat threshold; +0.4% YoY confirms no net QT acceleration; status supportive (flat to very slightly growing; no aggressive QT with rising overnight rates).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: VanEck mid-July 2026 Bitcoin ChainCheck reports perpetual funding rates at approximately +6.7% annualized over the prior week (equivalent to ~+0.006%/8h) and +4.5% annualized on a 30-day average (~+0.004%/8h); updated from prior run's +0.009%/8h as speculative positioning has moderated; BTC dominance 56.52% per TradingView Hub July 2026 data; CoinGlass returns HTTP 403 (proxy-blocked) again this run; 30-day trend down: funding rates declined from ~+0.009%/8h in late June to ~+0.006%/8h currently, indicating reduced leveraged long exposure consistent with spot-led price action; status supportive (current rates well below the 0.04% overheating threshold).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$304B (per CoinBird/TradingView Hub July 2026); total crypto market $2.27T; dominance: $304B / $2.27T = 13.4%; essentially unchanged from prior run ($305B / $2.28T = 13.4%); BTC dominance 56.52%; CoinGecko direct fetch 403; 30-day trend down: dominance was ~14.4% mid-June, 13.4% now—decline of ~100bps over 30 days sustained; status supportive (30-day downtrend intact; headwind condition 'rising while TOTAL also rising' not met—TOTAL $2.27T flat-to-slightly-down over 30 days while dominance declined).

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (June 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Durable Goods for June 2026 at 8:30 AM ET on Monday July 27—core capital goods orders (ex-defense, ex-aircraft) are the key business investment sub-component; first significant data release of the week, arriving one day before the two-day FOMC meeting begins July 28; a solid capex print alongside earlier soft CPI/PPI readings would reinforce the soft-landing case for a hold at 3.5–3.75%; weak orders could add downside risk to the growth outlook ahead of the July 30 Q2 GDP advance estimate.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence / FOMC Meeting Day 1 (July 28–29, 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—1-year inflation expectations sub-component watched for anchoring signals as the FOMC convenes; two-day FOMC meeting begins July 28 (Tuesday); rate decision and Chair Warsh press conference on July 29 at 2:00 PM ET / 2:30 PM ET—non-SEP meeting (no dot plot); current target range: 3.5–3.75%; note: H.6 M2 release July 28 implements new IRA/Keogh methodology adding ~$1T to reported M2; consensus strongly favors a hold; DXY at 101.47 and real yields at 2.37%—both above threshold, and a dovish tone is the primary macro catalyst.

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision & Press Conference (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve rate decision at 2:00 PM ET, Chair Warsh press conference at 2:30 PM ET—non-SEP meeting (no dot plot); current target range: 3.5–3.75%; consensus favors a hold; key watch: whether Warsh acknowledges back-to-back soft CPI and PPI prints as validating the disinflationary pipeline; a dovish hold could push DXY below 100 (currently 101.47) and compress real yields toward the 2.00% neutral threshold, potentially flipping both remaining macro headwinds and strengthening the BTC Accumulation setup; next SEP meeting: September 15–16; FOMC minutes from this meeting expected ~August 19, 2026.

upcoming.title: Q2 GDP Advance Estimate / June PCE / BOE Rate Decision / Jobless Claims
upcoming.note: BEA Q2 2026 GDP Advance Estimate at 8:30 AM ET—first official read on Q2 economic growth; BEA Personal Income and Outlays for June 2026 also at 8:30 AM ET—core PCE price index is the Fed's preferred monthly inflation gauge; Initial Jobless Claims (week ended July 26) also at 8:30 AM ET; Bank of England MPC decision at 12:00 BST (7:00 AM ET)—'Super Thursday' with full Monetary Policy Report and Governor's press conference at 1:00pm BST; Bank Rate currently at 3.75%; BOE voted 7-2 to hold at June meeting; also the day of the next WALCL H.4.1 release (week ending July 29); released the morning after the July 29 FOMC decision, providing an immediate test of the soft-landing thesis.

upcoming.title: BOJ Rate Decision / Employment Cost Index Q2 / UMich Consumer Sentiment Final (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan monetary policy statement released overnight ET (concluding the July 30–31 BOJ meeting)—BOJ Policy Rate currently 0.75% (highest since 1995); BOJ will assess whether JPY dynamics and global disinflation justify further policy normalization; Employment Cost Index Q2 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (BLS)—the Fed's preferred quarterly measure of labor cost inflation; a hot ECI would complicate the post-FOMC dovish narrative; University of Michigan Final Consumer Sentiment (July 2026) at 10:00 AM ET—final July read on 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations.
